description: The WORKS prop set — the industry/infrastructure vocabulary the audit's §5.4 requires every works place type to be described in (`shipyard`, `salt-pans`, `paddy-works`, `clay-pit-and-kiln`, `portage-slipway`, `bog-iron-bloomery`, `works-town`, `crystal-diggings`, `boatwright-yard`). There is no kiln, saltern, sluice-gate, winding-gear or hull-on-stocks mesh anywhere in the vault and none can be sourced, so this kit packages the vanilla pieces those descriptions must be built from: the blacksmith set (forge, workbench, bellows, sharpening wheel), the smelter and its coal (READ AS the kiln), tanning and drying and fish racks, hand/vendor carts and wheels, firewood stacks, the mine timber family (beams, planks, scaffold supports) and ore faces, the full stockade scaffold family (bases, tops, ramp, stairs, bridges, posts) for slipways/stocks/staging, the lumbermill WATER WHEELS, the farmhouse walkway gate boards (the only vanilla piece that reads as a SLUICE gate), dock steps/entry, and salt/basket/barrel/crate/sack/bucket/pitchfork/shovel/trough dressing for salt-pan and paddy terrain (the pans and bunds themselves are compiler-authored terrain and water, not meshes). Mud Mother Grove adds the Argonian fish rack, carapace oven, clay oven, baskets, urn and woven/snake fences so a works site reads Argonian. TROPICALISED: vanilla-backed textures resolve through Tropical Skyrim (vanilla filenames, texture-only — it ships no architecture meshes), so the vanilla-backed pieces read hot and wet instead of Nordic grey. That is the PIPELINE DEFAULT for every kit since 2026-09-09, not a key this config sets; a kit keeps the un-tropicalised vanilla art only by declaring `untropicalisedReason`. `clutter/stockade` is not covered by Tropical and uses the same textureAliases redirect as settlement-stilt-v1. Gap G3 (a nailed notice/licence board readable at arm's length — tapping licences, nailed price lists, toll posts and register boards) is closed by BM&V's `advertising_board`: a freestanding roofed notice pane 1.56 × 1.39 × 2.47 m whose posted papers are part of the authored mesh (`infopanel_papers`), so no paper piece has to be jammed onto it.

snapLogic.grid: None — these are freestanding props, not a tileset. Placement is by hand/compiler rule against the site, not by connector.
snapLogic.stockade-scaffold: The one family here that DOES snap, in vanilla's own logic: a `stockadescaffoldbase<n>sided01` footing carries a `stockadescaffoldtop<n>sided01` deck of the matching side count (`n` = how many faces are railed), joined between decks by `bridge01/02`/`bridgenarrow`, climbed by `ramp01` or `stairs01`, and propped by `basesupport01` and `toppost01/02`. Keep side counts consistent around a platform or railings gap.
snapLogic.mine-timbers: `minewoodbeam01-03` + `minewoodbeamshort01/02` + `minewoodplanks01-04` are vanilla's shoring vocabulary and are placed as a repeating rib along a tunnel or trench; `minescaffoldsupport01`/`minescaffoldbasesupport01(w)` are the vertical props.
snapLogic.reads: Documented substitutions this kit is the answer to: kiln = `smelter01` + `smelter01coal01` + firewood stacks + drying racks; sluice gate = `walkwaycwallgate01/02` set in a compiler-cut channel; slipway/hull-on-stocks = stockade scaffold + `minewoodbeam` rollers + dock steps, with an SBoT hull raised on them (hull comes from the boat pools, not this kit); winding gear = mine scaffold and a shored tunnel mouth; saltern = terrain pans dressed with `saltpile`, baskets, rakes (`pitchfork01`), `shovel01` and a `horsetrough01` store; water-wheel works = `lumbermill01waterwheel01/02`.
snapLogic.unitScale: Bethesda units; 0.0142240 m/unit. Measured extents in works-v1.kit.json.
snapLogic.notice-board: `bmv:advertising_board` is freestanding and self-supporting (two posts, shingled roof, papers nailed to the pane by its author). Place it standing on its own base, pane facing the approach, at the head of a quay, stage rail or toll post; never mount it on a wall or fuse it to a rail — nothing authored it to snap. Pane centre sits ~1.6 m up, i.e. eye height, which is what makes it readable at arm's length.
snapLogic.assemblies: Composites in this kit: `composite:works/stockade-scaffold-2stage` and `-3stage` freeze the one rule the vanilla scaffold family actually has — a base carries the next stage 2.73 m above itself, unrotated (template vanilla:t0019, 28 placements). Nothing else here is composited: bridges, ramps, stairs and props join platforms, and what they join is a site decision. Every single piece stays in the kit.

compose.note: Vanilla's stockade scaffold, two stages. Template vanilla:t0019 (28 placements): a `stockadescaffoldbase4sided01` footing carries the next identical stage exactly 2.73 m above itself, unrotated. That is the same rule this kit's `stockade-scaffold` prose states in words, measured. The bridges, ramps, stairs and props stay separate placements: what they join is a site decision, not a module.

The same 2.73 m stage rule (vanilla:t0019, 28 placements) run to three stages, ~8.2 m of staging in one parcel, with the railed deck top on the head of the stack (vanilla:t0061, 17 placements, puts a `stockadescaffoldtop0sided01` 2.73 m above its base for exactly this reason). Used where a slipway or hull-on-stocks needs height rather than footprint.
